A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same structured state-space duality work. The core sections, Algorithm 1, theorems, and Appendix A can be matched reliably. Text, equations, figures, and tables are readable; v2 adds Appendix B.

before.justification: V1 contains mathematical results, complexity analysis, schematic figures, and appendix proofs, but no original experimental or numerical outcomes.

after.justification: Appendix B reports original numerical equivalence, rank, and runtime experiments, WikiText-2 training results, and synthetic time-series regression results.

M1.justification: The diagonal dual construction and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix B.6 introduces a limited architectural adaptation, SSD-Mamba, integrating a learned input-independent diagonal core and direct input skip term into a Mamba architecture.

E1.justification: V1 has no empirical task coverage. V2 introduces Gaussian-input equivalence and scaling tests, time-varying diagonal dynamics, random-query/key softmax tests, WikiText-2 next-token prediction, and noisy mixture-of-decays regression.

E2.justification: V2 introduces evaluated comparators absent from v1: Ma's minimal Mamba implementation in Table 1, an N = 1 scalar baseline in B.7, and recurrence versus explicit masked-attention implementations in numerical equivalence and runtime comparisons. These are actual comparisons, beyond v1's citations and theoretical relationships.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces experimental protocols rather than revising existing v1 experiments. These include discrepancy and numerical-rank measurements, sequence-length timing sweeps, and WikiText-2 evaluation using 128-token windows, 5,000 training and 1,000 validation segments, and ten training epochs. B.7 adds a separate 60-epoch regression protocol evaluated with MSE.

E4.justification: New analyses test numerical equivalence under constant and time-varying dynamics, distinct versus duplicated decay modes, rank dependence on state dimension, runtime scaling, and softmax rank growth. B.7 also examines how changing state dimension affects convergence and validation error. V1 has no corresponding empirical analyses.

E5.justification: V2 introduces repeated-run and uncertainty reporting: B.1–B.2 report 1,000 seeds, WikiText-2 results average six seeds with standard-deviation bands, and runtime and regression plots also report variability. B.4 mentions three timing repeats and means over 100 runs without explaining their relationship. V1 contains no comparable statistical reporting.

E6.justification: All empirical outcomes are new, including discrepancies around 10^-14, runtime and rank trends, and regression learning curves. Table 1 reports best validation loss of 10.5 versus 9.7 and best validation accuracy of 9.5% versus 11.1% for Mamba versus SSD-Mamba. These are within-v2 comparisons, not performance improvements over v1. B.2–B.3's reported matrix ranks conflict with their stated kernel construction.

T1.justification: Remark 4.1 adds an explicit N = 2, T = 4 matrix example separating diagonal from scalar-identity expressiveness. Remark 4.2 adds a 4NTd FLOP-count claim, and Appendix A.2 explicitly states its contradiction premise of at least N + 1 new columns. The main definitions, theorem statements, and remaining appendix proofs are retained.

C1.justification: V1 presents higher-rank equivalence as proving a conjecture. V2 acknowledges that the underlying equivalence is known and frames its contribution as a self-contained constructive proof in causal SSM notation, narrowing the novelty claim. The abstract and other principal duality claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive qualifications about the absence of optimized diagonal-SSD kernels and the structural theorem's distinction from a practical training recipe. It also introduces interpretations of SSD-Mamba's validation behavior as reduced overfitting and additional state modes as facilitating optimization. Its new rank discussions incorrectly use full matrix rank to support conclusions about semiseparable rank.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's mathematical pseudocode, v2 supplies NumPy/PyTorch implementation descriptions, precision choices, synthetic-data construction, tokenization, vocabulary and sample limits, model dimensions, optimizer settings, and training budgets. It also adds a code-repository pointer on the title page. These disclosures principally support the newly added experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ma's implementation, Merity et al.'s dataset reference, and Sieber et al.'s analysis, connecting the latter to the softmax obstruction. It also acknowledges prior structured-matrix equivalence more explicitly. The broader related-work discussion is retained; consolidation of duplicate Gu et al. entries does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: The existing section order and most theoretical prose remain intact. V2 locally rewrites the novelty discussion and contribution bullet, adds explanatory remarks and cross-references, updates author and acknowledgment text, and extends the contents for Appendix B. The scientific expansion does not entail wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 1 and Figures 8–14, substantially expanding the visual presentation with runtime, rank, learning-curve, and state-dimension plots, including uncertainty bands. Original Figures 1–7 are retained, with some relocation and regrouping.

improvement.justification: V2 improves attribution, clarifies implementation limits, and adds a concrete expressiveness example and experimental documentation. However, B.2–B.3 report low full-matrix ranks for lower-triangular kernels with nonzero diagonals, which necessarily have rank T. B.5 likewise uses full matrix rank to infer semiseparable-rank limitations. These problems undermine the claimed empirical validation, leaving meaningful benefits and reliability harms without a confidently assessable net quality direction.
